To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epidermal dermo-epidermal junction is a specialized area of the epidermis that has a unique ultrastructure.

the basal cells are not connected to the basement membrane by desmosomes but rather that the membrane is a continuous layer of amorphous, dense material, and that the basal cell cytoplasm is not connected to the membrane but rather is separated from it by an electron-lucent space of variable width.

the basal cells of the epidermis and the epidermal-dermal junction are composed of two distinct layers, a superficial layer of cells with large numbers of tonofilaments and a deeper layer of cells with small numbers of tonofilament.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1.
the study of the epidermal basal cell and its relationship to the epidermal-dermal junction.
a study of the fine structure of the epidermis and its relation to the underlying dermis, particularly in the area of the dermal-epidermal junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron microscope has revealed many of the details of epidermal structure, but that the significance of these details has not been established.
the epidermal dermis junction is not an anatomically defined structure.

the epidermal basal cell is an undifferentiated cell with the capacity of producing the various cells of the epidermis, that it is in close contact with the dermis and that it is capable of producing a basal membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electron microscopic examination of the epidermis has not yet reached the stage where the results can be compared with the light microscopic observations.
, in general, the basal cells of the epidermis are similar to those of other epithelia.
the basal cells are more complex than the light microscope reveals and that the dermal epidermal junction is more complicated than the classical histologic description of the "rete" indicates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epidermis is a dynamic tissue, with the basal cell constantly dividing, and the keratinocyte constantly moving upwards.
we have a very good understanding of how the epidermal-dermal junction is formed.
the epidermis is an active, metabolically dynamic structure.
